shortlist.label: Cystoid macular edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe macular changes with associated edema and central macular thickness of 669.8 μm

shortlist.label: Central retinal vein occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of multiple strokes and vision loss in one eye, which are risk factors for CRVO

shortlist.label: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is 63 years old and has severe macular changes, which are consistent with neovascular AMD

shortlist.label: Diabetic macular edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are risk factors for diabetes and DME

shortlist.label: Branch retinal vein occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has vision loss in one eye and severe macular changes, which are consistent with BRVO

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of vision loss, severe macular changes, and associated edema, along with the spectral-domain optical coherence tomography findings showing persistent central macular thickness and changes in macular edema, are most consistent with cystoid macular edema, especially given the reversible effect on cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion after stopping niacin therapy as described in the image title and description.

rejected.label: Central retinal vein occlusion
rejected.why: While central retinal vein occlusion could lead to cystoid macular edema, it is not the most direct diagnosis based on the provided information, which focuses more on the edema itself rather than the occlusion event.

rejected.label: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration
rejected.why: There is no mention of neovascularization or age-related macular degeneration in the provided case facts, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Diabetic macular edema
rejected.why: There is no mention of diabetes in the patient's history, which is a key factor for diabetic macular edema.

rejected.label: Branch retinal vein occlusion
rejected.why: Similar to central retinal vein occlusion, branch retinal vein occlusion could lead to macular edema but is not directly indicated by the provided information, which does not specify the type of retinal vein occlusion or focus on the occlusion itself.
